belief: Strong emotions mean my faith is weak.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that strong emotions mean your faith is weak, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Being told as a child to stop crying or calm down. A church culture that valued always looking happy and peaceful. Hearing that a “real Christian” should never feel afraid, sad, or upset. A family where feelings were ignored or punished. Confusing strong feelings with a lack of trust in God.
teaches: God made us with emotions, and Scripture is full of people of strong faith who felt deeply. The psalmists poured out sorrow, fear, and confusion to God. Jesus was deeply troubled and distressed in Gethsemane. Paul admitted to fears within. Faith does not mean having no strong feelings; it means bringing those feelings to God and trusting Him with them.
self_statements: If I trusted God, I wouldn’t feel this way.
My feelings prove I’m spiritually weak.
I have to hide how I really feel.
God is disappointed when I’m upset.
errors: Concluding that strong feelings must mean weak faith.
“I should never feel afraid, sad, or angry.”
Calling yourself “weak” because you feel deeply.
Overlooking that bringing feelings to God is an act of faith.
Comparing your inner life to other people’s calm appearance.
questions: Did Jesus feel strong emotions? Was His faith weak?
What did the psalmists do with their sorrow and fear?
Does Psalm 62:8 tell me to hide my heart or pour it out?
Who taught me that feelings were bad or dangerous?
Can I feel afraid and still trust God at the same time?
What would change if I saw my emotions as something to bring to God?
Is faith about what I feel, or about whom I trust?
truth: Strong emotions do not mean my faith is weak. God made me with feelings, and Jesus Himself was deeply troubled. Faith is not the absence of strong feelings; it is bringing them honestly to God. I can pour out my heart to Him and trust Him at the same time.
hw_questions: What did the psalmists do with their feelings?
Does God tell me to hide my heart or pour it out?
Who taught me feelings were bad?
Can I feel afraid and still trust God?
Is faith about feelings or about whom I trust?
hw_truths: Strong feelings do not mean weak faith.
I can pour out my heart to God.
Jesus Himself was deeply troubled, and He understands.
I can feel afraid and still trust God.
Bringing my emotions to God is an act of faith.
log: Each day, name one strong feeling I had and write a short prayer pouring it out to God.
name_example: When Sarah is afraid, she puts her trust in You.
actions: describe exactly how you feel, then end with one line of trust, like the psalmists did.
Tell one safe person how you really feel
this week, without minimizing it, and notice what happens.
noticing how the writer moves between despair and hope.
When a strong feeling comes, pause and name it,
then pray one sentence about it instead of pushing it away.
tracker: One feeling I brought to God
prayer: Father, thank You for making me with feelings. Help me reject the lie that strong emotions mean my faith is weak. Teach me to pour out my heart to You, as the psalmists did and as Jesus did. When I am afraid or sad, help me put my trust in You. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
